sections.content: If you are looking for deeply discounted real estate deals, Youngstown, Ohio should be on your radar. This mid-sized Rust Belt city offers some of the lowest entry prices in the entire country, with median home prices sitting well below $80,000. For investors who know how to spot opportunity, that kind of affordability opens doors to strong cash flow, solid wholesale margins, and meaningful equity plays. Whether you are a seasoned flipper or just getting started — check out this Real Estate Investing for Beginners guide if you are new to the game — Youngstown deserves a serious look.
Youngstown OH Real Estate Market Overview

Youngstown sits in Mahoning County in northeast Ohio, about 75 miles southeast of Cleveland and 60 miles northwest of Pittsburgh. The city peaked in population around 170,000 in the 1930s during its steel industry heyday. Today the population hovers near 60,000, and that decades-long decline created a massive inventory of distressed, vacant, and undervalued properties. While that sounds like a negative, it is exactly the condition that creates the best buying opportunities for real estate investors. Home values have been slowly stabilizing since 2019, and with the national push to revitalize Rust Belt cities, Youngstown is seeing renewed attention from both local and out-of-state investors.
Average Home Prices and What Your Money Gets You

The median home price in Youngstown is approximately $65,000 to $75,000 as of 2024, making it one of the most affordable mid-sized markets in the U.S. Distressed and off-market properties regularly sell between $10,000 and $35,000, while move-in-ready single-family rentals can be acquired for $50,000 to $90,000. After renovation, many properties appraise between $90,000 and $130,000 in the best neighborhoods, leaving room for a healthy spread on flips and solid cash-on-cash returns for landlords. Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Youngstown

Not every zip code in Youngstown offers the same opportunity. Knowing which neighborhoods are stabilizing versus which are still declining is critical to protecting your investment. Here is a breakdown of the areas that consistently attract investor attention.

items: Boardman Township (44512): Technically a suburb just south of Youngstown proper, Boardman offers the highest home values in the metro area with medians near $120,000 to $150,000. Great for buy-and-hold rentals targeting working families and professionals.

Canfield and Poland (44406/44514): These southern suburbs are among the most stable in Mahoning County. Lower distress levels but consistent rental demand and strong resale values make these ideal for turnkey BRRRR strategies.

Brier Hill and Wick Park (44505): Located on Youngstown's near north side, Wick Park features some of the city's most beautiful historic architecture. Early investors who bought here 5 to 7 years ago have seen the strongest appreciation in the city.

Idora Neighborhood (44511): A west-side neighborhood that community groups and local investors have actively been rehabilitating. Entry prices are very low, and the trajectory is positive for long-term holds.

Austintown Township (44515): One of the most popular suburban destinations in the metro for renters. Single-family homes here rent for $800 to $1,100 per month and carry much lower vacancy risk than city proper properties.

sections.content: Pro Tip: Before buying in any Youngstown neighborhood, check the Mahoning County Land Bank website. The land bank actively acquires, manages, and sells vacant and blighted properties at reduced prices — sometimes for as little as $1,000 — and partnering with them can be one of the fastest ways to build a local portfolio.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Youngstown
Wholesale Deals

Wholesaling is extremely active in the Youngstown market because there is a high volume of distressed and vacant properties. Wholesale assignment fees typically range from $3,000 to $10,000 per deal, with some higher-value deals generating $12,000 to $15,000. The key is finding motivated sellers before they list publicly. To learn how to source these opportunities consistently, read our guide on How to Find Off-Market Real Estate Deals. Use our free Wholesale Deal Calculator to quickly confirm whether a property meets your buyer's criteria before locking it up under contract.
Fix and Flip

Flipping homes in Youngstown requires discipline on your rehab budget. Because ARVs are lower than in larger cities, you cannot afford to over-improve a property. The most successful Youngstown flippers target homes needing $15,000 to $40,000 in repairs that will sell for $90,000 to $130,000 after renovation. That leaves a workable margin when you buy right at $35,000 to $55,000. Focus on cosmetic flips — kitchens, bathrooms, flooring, paint, and curb appeal — and avoid deals that require foundation work or full gut renovations unless your acquisition price reflects that risk.
Buy and Hold Rentals

Cash flow is where Youngstown truly shines for the patient investor. A $60,000 single-family home in Austintown or Boardman can rent for $850 to $1,050 per month. After taxes, insurance, and a property management fee (typically 8 to 10 percent in this market), you can realistically net $400 to $600 per month in cash flow. That is a cash-on-cash return well above the national average. Multi-family properties — duplexes and four-plexes — are also widely available and can amplify these returns even further.

"The Rust Belt is the new Sun Belt for serious cash flow investors. You can buy three properties in Youngstown for the down payment you'd need on one deal in Phoenix — and the rent-to-price ratio tells the real story." — Common wisdom among Midwest real estate investors
Local Market Trends Investors Need to Know

Several trends are shaping the Youngstown market in 2024 and beyond. First, remote work has driven migration into affordable Midwest cities as workers flee high-cost coastal markets. Youngstown's proximity to Pittsburgh and Cleveland — both growing tech and healthcare hubs — makes it a logical destination. Second, Youngstown State University enrolls over 12,000 students annually, creating consistent demand for rental housing near campus on the city's east side. Third, Amazon, FedEx, and other logistics companies have opened distribution centers in the broader Mahoning Valley, bringing blue-collar employment that supports rental demand. These are all tailwinds that did not exist five to seven years ago.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

Investing remotely in a market like Youngstown is absolutely achievable, but it requires building the right local team and doing your due diligence upfront. Many out-of-state investors have built profitable portfolios here by following a systematic approach. Learn how to evaluate deals properly with our guide on How to Analyze Real Estate Deals Like a Pro before wiring any earnest money.

items: Build a local team first: You need a reliable property manager, a licensed inspector, a local real estate attorney, and at least one contractor you trust before closing your first deal. Interview at least three of each.

Never skip the inspection: Youngstown has a high number of aging properties with deferred maintenance. Old wiring, failing roofs, and cracked foundations are common. A $300 inspection can save you a $30,000 surprise.
Use the land bank as a resource: The Mahoning County Land Bank is investor-friendly and offers title-cleared properties that eliminate a major risk of buying distressed properties at auction.
Account for property taxes accurately: Mahoning County property taxes are moderate but vary significantly by municipality. Always confirm the tax bill before running your cash flow numbers.

Visit before you scale: Even if you eventually invest remotely, try to visit Youngstown at least once to drive neighborhoods, meet your team in person, and understand the physical condition of properties at different price points.

Study comparable sales carefully: With such a wide range of property quality in this market, comps can be misleading. Work with a local agent or appraiser who specializes in investment properties to validate your ARV assumptions.

Is Youngstown the Right Market for You?

Youngstown is not a market for investors chasing rapid appreciation or quick equity pops. It is a market for investors who want maximum cash flow, low entry costs, and the ability to build a sizeable portfolio without burning through capital. The risks are real — vacancy, property condition, and neighborhood quality vary enormously — but for disciplined investors who do their homework, the reward-to-risk ratio is hard to beat.
